what_happened: The task description's quoted yield (17 valid of 806 at complexity 4 over Base) counts 15 structural-prefilter decisions that carry no derivation at all; only 2 of the 17 have a proof_trace. The theorem-half yield of the tableau proper is ~12% of the headline valid_count (c4 2/17, c5 8/100, c6 42/790).

TheoremEntry.proof requires a DerivationTree schematic in all arguments, but no Formula-to-Formula uniform substitution exists as data anywhere in the tree -- only the L-to-L-plus substPlus/PlusDerivationTree.ofTMSubst. The ADMIT stage cannot be built without an L-level DerivationTree.subst.

Compile-verified that the missing L-level uniform substitution is a mechanical port of PlusDerivationTree.ofTMSubst: substF, Axiom.ofSubst (20 arms), Axiom.minFrameClass_ofSubst, substF_reflectTime and DerivationTree.subst all elaborate sorry-free, and register_theorem ACCEPTS a row built by generalizing a concrete derivation (profile box, arity 1, fragment ModalBoolean; axioms propext+Quot.sound).

scripts/proof-mode-cost-baseline.sh pins a measured surface that INCLUDES the directory BimodalLib/Diagnostics. Adding the five reserved-stage emitters there moves the surface head and makes the cost baseline stale: verified exit 3 ('STALE BASELINE') with a deliberately wrong --pin. Either site the new emitters outside that directory or narrow SURFACE to the three measured files.

Proof extraction is Base-only: extractProof ignores its frame-class argument (_fc) and ProofExtractionResult.success is hard-coded to DerivationTree .Base. So the description's 'at each frame class the tableau accepts' buys nothing on the theorem half; stronger classes change only which branches close, i.e. the countermodel half.

Two complexity-4 dataset artifacts disagree on the valid count: data/bmlogic-c4_metadata.json reports 17 valid / 669 invalid / 120 undetermined of 806, data/exhaustive_c4_metadata.json reports 13 / 673 / 120. Whichever figure the record quotes must name its artifact.

The gate-pass-rate probe (enumerate at bound 4, decide at Base and ZTime, evaluate the eight gates per invalid verdict) did not finish in 25 minutes and was stopped. evalBranchGates re-runs buildTableau for every invalid verdict, roughly doubling DECIDE cost; the per-cell gate pass rate is unmeasured and is the first figure the plan's opening phase should take.

Two copies of the gate-pass-rate probe ran concurrently for ~20 minutes. The first launch call failed on its PID-file write (an unquoted scratchpad variable resolved to /yield.pid, Permission denied) but had ALREADY backgrounded the lean job, so the relaunch added a second elaboration competing for the same cores; and killing the recorded PID only killed the subshell, leaving the timeout/lake/lean children alive. Both instances were found via pgrep and killed. Lesson: quote the scratchpad path variable, and kill the process GROUP or the timeout wrapper's own PID, not the subshell's.

Research report's compiled probe had already elaborated the full five-declaration L-level substitution construction AND run register_theorem on a generalized row, so the plan's critical-path phase is authored against a verified shape rather than a hypothesis.

readme-lint.sh Check 4's grandfathering is asymmetric and is NOT in context/project/lean4/patterns/plan-authoring-gate-collisions.md: BimodalTools/README.md (stale 2026-09-27), FormalSystem/README.md (stale 2026-10-02) and FormalSystem/ProofSystem/README.md (stale 2026-09-21) are pinned in scripts/readme-date-baseline.txt, so refreshing their Last-verified stamps UN-grandfathers them and fails the gate, while BimodalLib/README.md and BimodalLib/Theorems/README.md carry no baseline row and therefore MUST be refreshed on touch. Planned per-phase accordingly.

typst/generated/status.typ counts FormalSystem/, Tests/ and BimodalTools/ .lean lines but NOT BimodalLib/ (scripts/typst-status-counts.sh:202-207), while .githooks/pre-commit fires on any staged .lean path. A phase touching only BimodalLib/** therefore needs no status.typ regeneration; every phase touching FormalSystem/, BimodalTools/ or Tests/ does, commit-blocking.

Reading extractProof live showed its strategies (tryAxiomProof, matchDerived, buildCompositionalProof, enhancedSearch) are pure functions of the formula alone, with the tableau only gating the .allClosed branch. That opened a second admission route (elaboration-time extraction) which the plan then deliberately rejected in favour of source emission, on the ground that no native_decide is available and the kernel would have to reduce bounded proof search. The alternative is recorded as a Decision so it is not rediscovered mid-implementation.
